classification.difficultyReason: Students connect a zero derivative with separate constants on the two domain intervals, determine those constants using exact inverse-tangent values and represent the excluded origin in the sketch.

children.label: a
children.prompt: State the domain of $f(x)=\tan^{-1}x+\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$, and its symmetry.

answer.short: Domain: $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$. The function is odd, so its graph is symmetric about the origin.
answer.worked:
The term $\frac{1}{x}$ requires $x\ne0$, so the domain is $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$.
$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=\tan^{-1}(-x)+\tan^{-1}\left(-\frac1x\right)\\f(-x)&=-\tan^{-1}x-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac1x\right)\\f(-x)&=-f(x).\end{align*}$$
Thus $f$ is odd and its graph is symmetric about the origin.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that $f'(x)=0$ for all values of $x$ in the domain.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\pi}{2}&\text{for }x>0,\\-\dfrac{\pi}{2}&\text{for }x<0,\end{cases}$ and hence sketch the graph of $f(x)$.

answer.short: $f(x)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for $x>0$ and $f(x)=-\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for $x<0$. The graph has horizontal rays at these heights, with open endpoints at $x=0$.
answer.worked:
Since $f'(x)=0$, $f$ is constant on each of the intervals $(-\infty,0)$ and $(0,\infty)$ separately.
$$\begin{align*}f(1)&=\tan^{-1}1+\tan^{-1}1\\f(1)&=\frac\pi4+\frac\pi4\\f(1)&=\frac\pi2.\end{align*}$$
Thus $f(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}$ for $x>0$.
$$\begin{align*}f(-1)&=\tan^{-1}(-1)+\tan^{-1}(-1)\\f(-1)&=-\frac\pi4-\frac\pi4\\f(-1)&=-\frac\pi2.\end{align*}$$
Thus $f(x)=-\frac{\pi}{2}$ for $x<0$. There is no point on the graph at $x=0$.

spec.description: Two horizontal rays with open endpoints on the y-axis. The positive-height ray extends right and the negative-height ray extends left. Axes and curves use ordinary black marks; no grid or additional ticks.
spec.mathematics: y = pi/2 for x > 0 and y = -pi/2 for x < 0; x = 0 is excluded.
